workflows.name: linkedin-content
workflows.generate: Draft two LinkedIn posts for the upcoming Saturday slot: one founder-voice (Navid's personal page) and one Subturtle-voice (company page). Read the last ~10 published/drafted posts on each voice first and skip topic overlap. Follow the founder-post rules and Subturtle-page rules in the playbook for tone, length, structure and topics. Create each as a task titled 'LinkedIn (founder) — <topic>' or 'LinkedIn (Subturtle) — <topic>' in the Subturtle Content Marketing list, tagged 'linkedin' plus 'navid-page' or 'subturtle-page', status 'approval', notify Navid.

workflows.name: reddit-content
workflows.generate: Daily Reddit scan: draft value-only comments on fitting threads and answer real replies on posted comments, gated for approval. Scan the 6 non-Korean subs (languagelearning, EnglishLearning, LearnJapanese, Spanish, French, German) once a day. Check each sub's current self-promo/AI rules first. Draft 0-2 new top-level comment tasks total, only on threads where existing comments genuinely miss an angle Subturtle's approach would add - never force a draft to hit a quota. Also check the account's notifications/inbox (both old.reddit.com/message/inbox and www.reddit.com/notifications) for real replies-with-questions on previously posted comments, and draft an answer for each one that needs it - skip pure upvotes/agreement. Skip duplicates of pending drafts, already-well-covered threads, locked threads, or threads whose rules argue against the angle.
